proof_skeleton_nl: First force the generators into the irrelevant maximal ideal. Then finite-dimensionality makes the full ideal m-primary, so after localizing at m we obtain an m-primary ideal in the d-dimensional regular local ring S_m. Height of an m-primary ideal is d, and in a regular local ring height equals grade. Since the localized ideal is generated by exactly d elements and has grade d, the chosen generators form a regular sequence in the local ring. Finally, because the quotients are graded and the generators are homogeneous, injectivity can be checked after localization at m, so the local regularity implies the desired global regularity in S.

steps.derives: For every i in 1..d, the homogeneous element g_i lies in the homogeneous maximal ideal m=(x_1,...,x_d) of S.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L1 directly to the given sequence g_1,...,g_d and the hypothesis that S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k.

steps.derives: If I=(g_1,...,g_d), then I subseteq m, sqrt(I)=m, and in the localization R=S_m the ideal I R is mR-primary; equivalently R/I R is Artinian.
steps.trivial_justification: By A1, every generator g_i lies in m, so I subseteq m. The ideal I is homogeneous because it is generated by homogeneous elements. Therefore L2 applies to I and yields sqrt(I)=m together with the Artinian statement after localizing at m.

steps.derives: The localized ring R=S_m is a regular local ring of Krull dimension d.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the content of L3.

steps.derives: The ideal I R in the d-dimensional local ring R has height d.
steps.trivial_justification: A2 says that I R is mR-primary. A3 says that R is a Noetherian local ring of dimension d. Applying L4 to the local ring R and the ideal I R gives ht(I R)=d.

steps.derives: The ideal I R has grade d inside the regular local ring R.
steps.trivial_justification: By A3, R is regular local. By A4, ht(I R)=d. Applying L5 to the ideal I R shows grade_R(I R)=ht(I R)=d.

steps.derives: The sequence g_1/1,...,g_d/1 is a regular sequence in R=S_m; equivalently, for each i, the image of g_i/1 in R/(g_1/1,...,g_{i-1}/1) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: The ideal I R is generated by the d elements g_1/1,...,g_d/1. By A1 each g_i lies in m, hence each g_i/1 lies in the maximal ideal mR. By A5 the grade of I R is d, which equals the number of chosen generators. Therefore L6 applies with n=d and concludes that the chosen generating tuple g_1/1,...,g_d/1 is a regular sequence in R.

steps.derives: Fix any i in 1..d and set M_i = S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}). Then multiplication by g_i/1 is injective on the localization (M_i)_m.
steps.trivial_justification: By construction, (M_i)_m is canonically isomorphic to R/(g_1/1,...,g_{i-1}/1). Step A6 states precisely that g_i/1 is not a zero-divisor on this localized quotient. That statement is equivalent to injectivity of multiplication by g_i/1 on (M_i)_m.

steps.derives: For the fixed i, multiplication by g_i on M_i = S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is injective. Since i was arbitrary, for every i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor.
steps.trivial_justification: Each module M_i is finitely generated and graded over the positively graded ring S, and each g_i is homogeneous. By A7, multiplication by g_i is injective after localizing M_i at m. L7 then implies that multiplication by g_i is already injective on M_i itself. Interpreting injectivity in the quotient ring language gives the required non-zero-divisor statement for this i, and hence for all i.

steps.derives: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d are homogeneous elements of S and S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k, then for each i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
steps.trivial_justification: The hypothesis is exactly the root hypothesis, and A8 gives exactly the required conclusion for each i. The final sentence is the definition of a homogeneous regular sequence for homogeneous elements.
